questions.question: Explain the difference between forward and reverse substitution using the car-hire formula, and how you recognise which one a question is asking for.
questions.expected_answer: Forward substitution: the input (kilometres) is known and slots into the right-hand side; compute directly to find the cost. Reverse: the output (cost) is known, so after substituting it on the left, the unknown must be dug out using inverse operations. Recognise the direction by asking which variable the question gives and which it wants.

questions.question: Why must the fixed charge be subtracted before dividing by the rate in the reverse question? Explain in money language, not just algebra.
questions.expected_answer: The R1 200 budget first pays the R450 fixed fee, which buys no distance at all; only the remaining R750 purchases kilometres. Dividing the whole budget by R12,50 pretends all R1 200 bought driving, giving an inflated 96 km instead of the true 60 km.

questions.question: Describe how you would verify each type of answer — the R4 700 forward answer and the 60 km reverse answer.
questions.expected_answer: For the forward answer, sense-check the size (the distance charge should dominate on a long trip) and confirm units. For the reverse answer, substitute 60 back into the formula: 450 + 12,50 × 60 = 1 200, which matches the budget exactly — the machine run forwards proves the backwards answer.
